A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same particle-guided diffusion work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE reconstruction experiments, noisy two- and three-species reaction–diffusion results, runtime measurements, and particle-count ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original forward/inverse PDE evaluations, noisy reaction–diffusion experiments, and empirical tempering and effective-sample-size analyses.

M1.justification: The residual likelihood, GEM and SOSaG proposals, TDS/pBS weighting, and Appendix A.1–A.4 pseudocode and derivations are unchanged. Tempering was already defined in v1 Equation (20); evaluating additional values does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: The same five benchmark PDEs remain, but v2 replaces their main joint-reconstruction evaluation with separate forward and inverse tasks observing only one field, as clarified in Section 4.2 and Table 1. Joint reaction–diffusion inference and its four observation-noise levels remain.

E2.justification: DiffPDE-NoG is removed from both experimental suites. GEM-TDS enters the reaction–diffusion comparison, where v1 explicitly omitted it after reporting equivalence with pBS. Standalone GEM already appeared as EM (Proposal) in v1 Appendix C, so its main-table appearance is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark particle budget changes from eight to four. v2 explicitly reports Darcy inverse error rate instead of v1's uniformly described relative errors, and introduces a six-setting tempering sweep from 5 to 1000. These protocol revisions prevent direct interpretation of benchmark score differences as performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds tempering sensitivity experiments and expands ESS analysis across proposals, forward/inverse tasks, and noisy reaction–diffusion systems. It removes v1's observation-likelihood weighting comparison and particle-count ablation. The equal-computation table primarily redisplays standalone-proposal results already represented in the comparisons.

E5.justification: v1 reports standard deviations throughout its performance tables; v2 removes these tabulated uncertainties despite retaining prose referring to subscripts. The main benchmark run count changes from 100 to 30. The new tempering table specifies 20 runs, and ESS plots retain shaded variability.

E6.justification: Benchmark and reaction–diffusion scores and reconstruction examples are extensively replaced, runtime results disappear, and tempering results are added. For 3SRD u at noise 0.02, v1 reports GEM-pBS 0.59% versus DiffPDE 3.34%; v2 reports 0.89% versus 0.79%, reversing their ranking. These are revised reported outcomes, not established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The principal mathematical formulation and target derivations remain unchanged. The ESS limiting argument changes from v1 Appendix A.5's beta approaching zero to v2 Appendix A.6's tempering parameter rho approaching infinity. This is a limited revision of mathematical reasoning, without a new convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 contribution list are unchanged. They retain the claims of SMC-based PDE guidance, the SOSaG proposal, a consistency–performance tradeoff, and superior reconstruction across benchmark and interacting PDE systems.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.5 reframes pBS as exact sampling from a calibrated alternative target rather than an exactness–performance tradeoff. v2 also expands the evolutionary-algorithm interpretation, identifies problem-specific tempering and deterioration at excessive values, and acknowledges strong DiffPDE solution-field performance instead of v1's broad inferiority account.

D1.justification: New Table 5 discloses per-PDE observation and residual guidance weights, and Appendix B.2 explains joint-weight tuning against overall residual error. Architecture, training-data counts, training iterations, A100 hardware, and 2000 sampling steps remain documented as before. The new disclosures do not establish changed training.

R1.justification: v2 adds Del Moral (2004) and Jiang et al. (2026), and discusses Wu et al.'s tempering precedent. References supporting the removed particle-count discussion—Chopin (2004), Meyn and Tweedie, and Robert et al.—disappear. The main positioning against DiffusionPDE and earlier SMC guidance remains.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose and the main section order are retained. Discussion and limitations are revised, the evolutionary-algorithm explanation is expanded, Appendices A and C gain subsections, and method labels are standardized. Correspondence and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a full-width forward/inverse comparison grouped by sampler type, and reaction–diffusion summaries receive a separate table. Reconstruction and error figures are extensively redrawn with reordered methods, ground truth, field labels, and color scales. New tempering and ESS displays replace the earlier ESS presentation and likelihood schematic.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful forward/inverse evaluations, tempering and ESS evidence, and reproducibility information through guidance weights. However, it removes standard deviations, measured runtimes, and particle-count and likelihood-weighting ablations. Its new exactness framing is not reconciled with the retained introductory tradeoff claim, and some captions and statistical prose remain outdated. These material gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment; changed settings also prevent treating revised scores as accuracy improvements.
